rationale: Close the recorded limitation that the periodic-heartbeat batching path was source-only. The same harness now queues two follower reads and lets one ordinary leader tick produce the confirmation heartbeat, with no harness-chosen delivery order: the heartbeat carries the newest queued context, the reply to the earlier requester carries that newest context at the confirmed index, and the earlier requester's batch stays at index zero after the ready index is applied. A single-read case uses the same tick-driven path and completes, so the difference is the batching of an earlier request into a newer confirmation rather than the tick path itself. The harness file is the one used by the observer-endpoint experiment, extended with these two cases, so this is a fresh execution of a revised experiment.

experiment.revision_reason: Add a tick-driven periodic-heartbeat case with two queued reads and a single-read control, so the batching path recorded from source is measured rather than assumed.

scope.description: Tick-driven ReadIndex batching. Two follower-originated ReadIndex requests are queued at the real leader of a three-voter in-process group, one ordinary leader tick produces the confirmation heartbeat, and the earlier requester's reply and pending-read completion are measured; a second case queues one read and runs the same tick path.
assumptions: The voter group is three real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3}; node 1 is leader and each node uses a test-only in-memory ILogDB.
Both reads are registered through the real node-level pendingReadIndex and forwarded by the real follower ReadIndex path.
The only scheduling input is one leader tick; the harness does not choose which heartbeat is delivered first or reorder any message.
The single-read control uses the same setup, the same tick path and the same consumer, with one queued request instead of two.
excluded: No NodeHost, transport, persistence, restart or snapshot path is exercised.
No proposal or membership change is made while the reads are outstanding.
The run observes reply-context association and pending-read completion only; it does not attempt to establish a stale data value.

experiment.prefix: The harness launches three real Raft peers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and ticks node 1 until its current-term no-op is committed. Node 2 and node 3 each register a node-level pending read under a generated context and forward it to the leader through the real follower path, so both requests sit in the leader's readIndex queue. The harness then calls Tick once on the leader and pumps it; the produced heartbeat addressed to node 3 carries the newest queued context. That heartbeat is delivered to node 3, whose echo is returned to the leader, and the leader's replies are collected. The reply addressed to node 2 is emitted with its response context and log index, delivered to node 2's real handler, and the resulting ReadyToRead plus that log index are fed to pendingReadIndex.addReady and pendingReadIndex.applied; the run records the batch index and whether the read completed. The control case repeats the setup with only node 2's read queued, ticks the leader once, delivers the heartbeat carrying that single context, and records the same reply and completion fields.
experiment.requirement: A leader-produced confirmation heartbeat must not cause an earlier queued ReadIndex request to be answered with a different request's SystemCtx, and the earlier requester's admitted read must complete once the confirmed index is applied.
experiment.responsibility: leaderTick and broadcastHeartbeatMessage choose the context carried by the periodic heartbeat, handleLeaderHeartbeatResp feeds the echoed hint to handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation, and that handler builds each remote reply; the requesting node's pendingReadIndex consumes it. The experiment exercises those real handlers and changes only how many reads are queued before the tick.

comparisons.description: When a leader tick confirms the newest of two queued reads, the reply delivered to the earlier requester must still carry the context that requester admitted.
After the confirmed index is applied, the earlier requester's admitted read should complete.
With one queued read, the tick-driven reply must carry that read's own context.
With one queued read, the same tick-driven path should complete it.
